title: Expositione in Paschale Carmen
author: Remigius of Auxerre
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0241d.stoa002.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's CSEL and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Si ergo nos dimiserimus fratribus nostris minora, dimittet nobis deus maiora, si non, nectemur grauius iam soluti a peccatis. Hic tangit euangelium, ubi legitur homo quidam posuit rationem cum seruis suis\'. Donec finitum pro infinito posuit, quia illi qui in inferno damnandi sunt, nunquam ueniam merebuntur, non sicut Origenes dicit, post mille annos soluetur satanas cum suis, sed magis sententia domini cauta erit, qua dicit \'ibunt impii in suppli. cium aeternum*. Ergo donec pro semper posuit, sicut in psalmo legitur \'ita oculi nostri ad dominum deum nostrum, donec misere- atur nostri semper. Breuem minimum. Amen. Haec , particula signum et quoddam sigillum est dominicae orationis, quo confirmantur omnia, quae supra dicta sunt. Malum diabolum. Bonum Christum, deum adimus non gressu corporis sed intentione mentis, deo enim non loco sed mente approximamus aut elongamus.
passages.english: If, then, we forgive our brothers the lesser [debts], God will forgive us the greater; if not, we shall be bound more heavily, though already released from sins. Here he touches on the Gospel, where one reads, 'a certain man settled accounts with his servants.' 'Until': he has put the finite for the infinite, because those who are to be damned in hell will never merit pardon, not as Origen says, that after a thousand years Satan will be released with his own, but rather the sentence of the Lord will be sure, in which he says, 'the wicked will go into eternal punishment.' Therefore he has put 'until' for 'always', as is read in the psalm, 'so our eyes [are] toward the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us', [that is] always. 'Brief': very small. 'Amen': this particle is a sign and a kind of seal of the Lord's Prayer, by which everything said above is confirmed. 'Evil': the devil. 'Good': Christ. We approach God not by the step of the body but by the intention of the mind, for we draw near to God or move far from him not by place but by mind.
passages.notes: Lemmata (words glossed from the poem) are given as quoted words. 'Breuem minimum' is a terse gloss, rendered literally. 'suppli. cium' and 'misere- atur' are scanning splits.

passages.original: Ista enim die transierunt filii Israel ex Aegypto. Pascha autem erat apud Iudeos agnus, qui immolabatur ad uesperum. Gloria maiestas Christi. Pulchra locutio est, quando pro persona per circumlocutionem declaratur qualitas, ut Virgilius \'robur Troianorum\' Hector, ita dicitur gloria domini Christus. Clarificem in resurrectione. Consonam consors; quia patrem uocauerat, respondit ei pater. Ita uox non fnit dei patris substantialiter, sicut columba non fuit Spiritus sanctus nec ex aliis columbis generata, sed ex aere, ita ista nox non fuit patris substantialiter, sed signum ut demonstraretur Christus filius dei.
passages.english: For on that day the children of Israel passed out of Egypt. Among the Jews, the Pascha was the lamb that was sacrificed in the evening. 'Glory': the majesty of Christ. It is a fine figure of speech when, in place of a person, a quality is expressed by circumlocution, as Virgil [says] 'the strength of the Trojans' [for] Hector; so Christ is called the glory of the Lord. 'May I glorify': in the resurrection. 'In harmony': sharing; because he had called on the Father, the Father answered him. So the voice was not substantially that of God the Father; just as the dove was not the Holy Spirit, nor born from other doves but [formed] from the air, so this voice was not substantially the Father's, but a sign, so that Christ might be shown [to be] the Son of God.
passages.notes: 'fnit' read as 'fuit'; 'nox' in the last sentence read as 'uox' (voice), evidently a scanning or printing error.
